Document 1247: Troy will turn off ShotSpotter
TROY — The cops on the beat, the brass and the mayor all agree that the high-tech listening system that's supposed to identify the location of gunshots is ineffective.
特洛伊市——无论是巡逻警察、警局高层还是市长，都一致认为那个旨在识别枪击位置的高科技监听系统是无效的。
That's why the city has decided to get rid of the ShotSpotter system at the end of the year.
"We are discontinuing Shot-Spotter," Chief [John Tedesco](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22John+Tedesco%22) said Tuesday night during the [Public Safety Committee](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Public+Safety+Committee%22)'s review of the police department budget for 2013.
这就是为什么该市决定在年底停用ShotSpotter系统。
Dropping the system means the city will save $39,000 in annual costs. Tedesco said the company had been pressuring the department to upgrade the system, which would have moved monitoring to California instead of in police headquarters.
The displeasure with the acoustic surveillance system is so prevalent that Tedesco and Officer [Robert Fitzgerald](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Robert+Fitzgerald%22), the [Troy Police Benevolent Association](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Troy+Police+Benevolent+Association%22) president, who usually disagree on issues, both agree that it's time is over.
“我们将停用ShotSpotter，”局长约翰·特德斯科周二晚间在公共安全委员会审查警察局2013年预算时表示。
"We're getting a better response from the public," Fitzgerald said about calls residents made to report gunfire.受影响方
The chief and union president said the patrol officers supported dumping ShotSpotter.
放弃该系统意味着该市每年将节省3.9万美元的开支。特德斯科表示，该公司一直向警局施压要求升级系统，而升级本会将监控工作转移至加利福尼亚州，而非保留在警察总部。
Tedesco said the system never achieved what it was suppose to do when the city installed it for $250,000 in 2009 using drug forfeiture money to cover the cost.
"It wasn't reliable," Tedesco said.
对这套声学监控系统的反感非常普遍，以至于平日里在诸多问题上意见相左的特德斯科与特洛伊警察慈善协会主席罗伯特·菲茨杰拉德警官，都一致认为该系统已到了该退场的时候。
It also was expensive, the chief said. Moving one of the listening devices, he said, cost $6,500.
The system was suppose to become attuned to the way sounds were heard in Troy's streets and differentiate among the brakes of a truck climbing the Hoosic Street hill, from a firecracker, actual shots and any other noise.
“公众的反应更好，”菲茨杰拉德在谈到居民拨打枪击报警电话时如是说。
Tedesco said this was never completely achieved.
Mayor [Lou Rosamilia](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Lou+Rosamilia%22) said he backed the decision to end participation in ShotSpotter.
局长和工会主席均表示，巡逻警员支持弃用ShotSpotter。
"It's not working in the way it's suppose to," Rosamilia said.
A ShotSpotter spokeswoman could not be immediately reached Tuesday night for comment.
特德斯科表示，2009年该市利用毒品没收资金出资25万美元安装该系统时，它就从未实现过预期的功能。
Troy installed a network of 22 acoustic listening devices to cover the neighborhoods with the highest crime incidents.
The city rolled out the surveillance devices with great fanfare in late 2008. It was supposed to lead officers to the sites where shots were fired when not reported by the public.
“它不可靠，”特德斯科说。
Rosamilia, Tedesco and Fitzgerald each said that unlike in some cities, Troy residents call in reports of gunshots.
At first, police touted the system as an early success. Each patrol car had access to the computerized monitoring system installed to allow officers to get the information firsthand.
局长还表示，该系统成本也很高。他说，移动其中一个监听设备的费用就高达6500美元。
It was expected to take a full year to fine-tune the acoustic devices so it would pick out the gunshots from other sounds. Tedesco said that never occurred.
The listening devices were placed to cover an area that ran from Lansingburgh south through downtown and into South Troy. The system also picked up sounds from the [Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Rensselaer+Polytechnic+Institute%22) campus.
该系统本应适应特洛伊街道上的声音特征，并区分爬霍西克街山坡的卡车刹车声、鞭炮声、真实的枪声以及其他任何噪音。
Retired Chief [Nicholas Kaiser](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Nicholas+Kaiser%22) pushed for the installation of the system, which was supported by former Mayor [Harry Tutunjian](https://www.timesunion.com/search/?action=search&channel=local&inlineLink=1&searchindex=solr&query=%22Harry+Tutunjian%22).
Document 2626: Controversial ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology failed to pick up two recent deadly shootings in Durham
A pair of deadly shootings [recently](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) went undetected by ShotSpotter, the [controversial](https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2022/10/durham-shotspotter-pilot-controversial-gunshot-detection-technology-in-november-community-members-express-concerns) gunshot detection technology currently being piloted by the city of Durham. A spokesperson for the Durham Police Department [told](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) CBS17 that police did not receive an alert for a Feb. 5 [shooting](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/1-shot-and-killed-in-durham-neighborhood-police-say/) at Fay and Juniper Streets and a [shooting](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-investigating-fatal-shooting-on-park-avenue/) last Thursday on Park Avenue. Both shootings resulted in two total deaths.
最近发生的两起致命枪击案未被ShotSpotter侦测到，这是达勒姆市目前正在试点的这项备受争议的枪声侦测技术。达勒姆警察局发言人告知CBS17，警方没有收到关于2月5日发生在Fay街和Juniper街交汇处的枪击案以及上周四发生在Park Avenue的枪击案的警报。这两起枪击案共造成两人死亡。
These reports come a month after a drive-by [shooting](https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2023/01/durham-shotspotter-technology-failed-to-notify-police-of-new-years-day-drive-by-shooting) on New Year’s Day that injured five people also went undetected by ShotSpotter. All three shootings fell within the three square miles that Shotspotter was monitoring. The area [represents](https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2022/10/durham-shotspotter-pilot-controversial-gunshot-detection-technology-in-november-community-members-express-concerns) only 2.7% of the total landmass of the city, but accounts for roughly one in three gunshot wounds.
Durham Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton, an early [advocate](https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2022/04/shotspotter-durham-chicago-charlotte-gun-violence-prevention-technology) for piloting the technology in Durham, defended its continued usage. He [said](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) to CBS17 that it was important to “look at all of the data” given the initiative is currently only two months into the year-long pilot.
这些报告发布前一个月，元旦当天发生的一起造成五人受伤的驾车枪击案也未被ShotSpotter侦测到。这三起枪击案均发生在ShotSpotter监测的三平方英里区域内。该区域仅占全市总面积的2.7%，但约占枪伤案件的三分之一。
“Any specific data point where we miss something is bothersome and disturbing, but we have to keep in mind that this is a piece of technology. My cell phone dropped a call last week, I’m not throwing my cell phone out.” Middleton [told](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) CBS17.
According to its monthly [report](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) for January, ShotSpotter sent the Durham Police 197 alerts, detecting 998 rounds fired. In its [contract](https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/crime/article265506381.html) with the city, ShotSpotter commits to detecting and locating 90% of unsuppressed outdoor gunfire when the fired rounds are above .25 caliber.
达勒姆临时市长马克-安东尼·米德尔顿曾是达勒姆试点该技术的早期支持者，他为其继续使用进行了辩护。他对CBS17表示，鉴于该项目目前仅处于为期一年的试点期的第二个月，重要的是“查看所有数据”。
Durham County [began](https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/counties/durham-county/article269993447.html) its one-year pilot of ShotSpotter last December. The system relies on sensors placed on buildings that can flag sounds that might be gunfire or explosions. The audio is then sent to ShotSpotter’s “Incident Review Center” where it is manually confirmed. Pollice can then be sent to the area.
“We are sending our deepest condolences to the community impacted by the recent shooting that took place in Durham, NC. We have investigated the situation and provided a report to the Durham Police Department,” the company [wrote](https://www.cbs17.com/news/local-news/durham-county-news/durham-police-did-not-receive-shotspotter-alerts-in-recent-deadly-shootings-officers-say/) in a statement.
“任何我们漏掉的具体数据点都令人烦恼和不安，但我们必须记住这是一项技术。上周我的手机掉线了，但我并没有把手机扔掉。”米德尔顿告诉CBS17。
Last September, the Durham school board [voted](https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/counties/durham-county/article266235211.html) to prohibit ShotSpotter from installing its sensors on school campuses. One board member deemed it an “item of surveillance.” Local residents have also [raised](https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2022/10/durham-shotspotter-pilot-controversial-gunshot-detection-technology-in-november-community-members-express-concerns) concerns that the technology may result in an increased police presence that could make racial profiling a more prevalent issue.
Document 3844: Gunshot Detection System Wastes N.Y.P.D. Officers’ Time, Audit Finds
ShotSpotter, a system the Police Department uses to detect gunfire, is overwhelmingly inaccurate and leads officers to spend hundreds of hours each month investigating nonexistent shots风险源, according to an [audit the New York City comptroller released Thursday](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/audit-report-on-the-new-york-city-police-departments-oversight-of-its-agreement-with-shotspotter-inc-for-the-gunshot-detection-and-location-system/#_ftn5).
据纽约市审计长周四发布的一份审计报告显示，警方用于侦测枪声的ShotSpotter系统极其不准确，导致警员每月花费数百小时调查根本不存在的枪击事件。
The Police Department has spent more than $45 million on ShotSpotter since it [started using it in 2015](https://www.nytimes.com/2015/03/17/nyregion/shotspotter-detection-system-pinpoints-gunshot-locations-and-sends-data-to-the-police.html), even as cities around the country have stopped using the system. New York must decide before December whether to renew its contract with SoundThinking, the California company that owns the system, and the audit advises officials to decline until the system can be fully evaluated.
Auditors studied ShotSpotter's accuracy over several months in 2022 and 2023. When it was performing at its best, only 20 percent of ShotSpotter's alerts actually revealed shootings, they found. Often, it did even worse. Of the 940 alerts officers responded to last June, only 13 percent corresponded to confirmed shootings.
自2015年开始使用ShotSpotter以来，警方已在该系统上花费超过4500万美元，尽管全美各地已有城市停止使用该系统。纽约必须在12月之前决定是否与拥有该系统的加州公司SoundThinking续签合同，而审计报告建议官员在对该系统进行全面评估之前拒绝续约。
And in 2022, the audit found, the system also failed to detect more than 200 real incidents of gunfire in Manhattan.
The Police Department "is wasting precious time and money on this technology and needs to do a better job managing its resources," the comptroller, Brad Lander, said in a statement. "Chasing down car backfires and construction noise does not make us safer."
审计人员对ShotSpotter在2022年和2023年数月间的准确性进行了研究。他们发现，即使在该系统表现最佳的时候，也只有20%的警报最终证实是枪击事件。通常情况下，其表现甚至更差。在去年6月警员响应的940起警报中，只有13%对应了经证实的枪击事件。
Several [major cities](https://www.cnn.com/2024/02/24/us/shotspotter-cities-choose-not-to-use/index.html) have moved away from ShotSpotter in recent years and others are grappling with whether to renew contracts that will expire this year. Chicago's mayor [campaigned](https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/shotspotter-ordinance-delayed-city-council-mayor-brandon-johnson/) on a promise to jettison the technology and blamed it for the death of an unarmed 13-year old shot by [officers responding to an](https://theintercept.com/2021/04/13/chicago-police-killing-boy-adam-toledo-shotspotter/) alert in 2021. In Boston, the mayor and the police department are [on the defensive](https://www.bostonherald.com/2024/05/24/amid-pushback-boston-mayor-wu-backs-police-use-of-shotspotter-technology/) after three members of the state's congressional delegation [signed a letter](https://www.bostonherald.com/2024/05/14/warren-markey-pressley-follow-boston-police-review-by-pressing-for-federal-probe-of-shotspotter/) that called for a national probe into the system.
The Police Department's press office declined to comment Thursday, referring to a response to the audit in which the department disputed some aspects of the report, saying that the comptroller's office had classified reports as unfounded if investigators found no physical evidence of gunfire. But that, the department said, did not mean shootings had not happened.
此外，审计发现，2022年该系统还未能侦测到曼哈顿发生的200多起真实枪击事件。
A spokeswoman for Mayor Eric Adams, Kayla Mamelak, called ShotSpotter "one of many tools we use to help fight crime to keep our city safe."
"While we understand that emerging technologies evolve and there is always room for improvement, what seems to be lost on the comptroller is that ShotSpotter has given the N.Y.P.D. the ability to solve countless crimes and save lives," she said in a statement.
审计长布拉德·兰德在一份声明中表示：“警方正在这项技术上浪费宝贵的时间和金钱，并且需要更好地管理其资源。追踪汽车回火声和建筑噪音并不能让我们更安全。”
In a statement Thursday, Jerome Filip, a spokesman for SoundThinking, dismissed the audit as a "gravely misinformed in its assessment of data" and said it emphasized the wrong metrics for evaluating the tool.
The company's shares [have lost nearly half their value](https://ir.soundthinking.com/stock-info/quote) this year.
近年来，已有几个主要城市弃用了ShotSpotter，其他城市也在纠结是否续签将于今年到期的合同。芝加哥市长在竞选时承诺摒弃该技术，并指责其导致了一名手无寸铁的13岁少年在2021年因警员响应警报而被枪杀。在波士顿，在该州国会代表团的三名成员签署联名信呼吁对该系统进行全国性调查后，市长和警方正处于守势。
ShotSpotter uses sensors that are installed across all five boroughs in New York. The devices listen for sharp, loud sounds and transmit data to staff members who determine whether they sound like gunshots and notify the police. According to [SoundThinking's website](https://www.soundthinking.com/law-enforcement/leading-gunshot-detection-system/), the process should take around a minute.
The audit said that most reports were erroneous and that officers rarely determined what had triggered false alarms. Common culprits are fireworks and street noise, it said. Those false alerts are costly: Officers spent almost 427 hours investigating unconfirmed reports in a single month, the audit found.
警方新闻办公室周四拒绝置评，而是引用了其对审计报告的回应。在该回应中，警方对报告的某些方面提出了异议，称审计长办公室在调查人员未发现枪击实物证据的情况下，就将报告归类为无根据。但警方表示，这并不意味着枪击事件没有发生。
The audit suggested that such fruitless work might be contributing to the [ballooning millions of dollars in overtime](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/overtime-overview/) that police officers claim each year. The Police Department disputed that, saying that only officers who are already on the clock respond to ShotSpotter alerts.
Civil liberties [groups say](https://www.aclu.org/news/privacy-technology/four-problems-with-the-shotspotter-gunshot-detection-system) that the listening devices, which are concentrated in areas where shootings often occur, can lead to overpolicing in low-income neighborhoods that are predominantly home to people of color. The groups also say that prosecutors use the system's questionable data to construct flimsy cases against people who have been accused of wrongdoing.
市长埃里克·亚当斯的发言人凯拉·马梅拉克称ShotSpotter是“我们用来打击犯罪、维护城市安全的众多工具之一”。
Daniel Schwarz, a technology and privacy strategist for the New York Civil Liberties Union, said that he hoped the audit would start a conversation about how the technology is used in New York.
"We know already that these sensors are primarily deployed in communities of color --- and we also know from the tragic killing in Chicago of Adam Toledo that ShotSpotter can escalate police violence," said Mr. Schwarz, adding that "it's on the N.Y.P.D. to really justify their reasoning behind the technology and why that technology is needed*."*
她在一份声明中表示：“虽然我们明白新兴技术会不断发展，且总有改进空间，但审计长似乎忽略了这一点：ShotSpotter赋予了纽约警方侦破无数案件和挽救生命的能力。”
In its response, the department said that letting the contract lapse would result in a "less safe working environment for officers and an increased chance of violent encounters for all New Yorkers."

Document 4366: Teacher’s shock discovery: Close friend responsible for sharing her deepfake porn images
**WARNING: This story discusses details of sexual abuse**
**警告：本文包含性虐待的相关细节**

Still skeptical, Hannah and her partner, Kris, clicked on the link. What they found was far worse than anything they could have imagined.
随后，一封改变一切的邮件来了。它来自另一位女性，另一位受害者。
"The link took us to this website. It's been taken down since, but it was like a forum, a thread like Reddit. My thread was called 'The Destruction of Hannah', and it had thousands of posts. Different men were posting, and they'd started a poll where they were voting on how best to rape me. The photos were pornographic images of real women, but they had superimposed my face onto their bodies. Some were really crude, but others used AI, and there were even GIFs, moving images of violent porn with my face on them."
"The images were mostly made up of incredibly violent porn, women tied up and beaten, with bruises added to my face. It was so terrifying that my brain just said, to keep me safe, I cannot see any more of this website. We later found out there were 600 posts of me. But scrolling through that first thread it's a shock that someone can spend that time so fixated on you," Hannah said.
“我收到一位女士的邮件，她说，‘汉娜，我觉得这种事也发生在你身上了，’”她回忆道。“她说有人在网上发布我的照片，是悉尼大学的某个人，还说她会继续给我发邮件，因为这非常重要。她提醒我，她发送的链接包含令人不安的图片。”
But the horror deepened when Hannah realised the personal nature of the images; whoever accessed the photos of her must be in her friend circle.
"I instantly thought, 'How did this person get these photos of me?' I've been a high school teacher for over a decade, so my social media has been locked down for 13 years. I knew right away, it had to be someone I knew. And just knowing that this person was clearly one of my friends was terrifying, though I never imagined for a moment that it would be someone very close to me."
尽管心存疑虑，汉娜和她的伴侣克里斯还是点击了那个链接。他们发现的情况比想象中任何可能的事情都要糟糕得多。
The betrayer revealed.
----------------------
“链接把我们带到了一个网站。虽然现在已经被关闭了，但当时它就像一个论坛，一个类似Reddit的帖子。关于我的帖子标题是‘汉娜的毁灭’，里面有数千条回复。不同的男人在上面发帖，他们发起了一项投票，表决如何最好地强奸我。照片是真实女性的色情图像，但他们把我的脸移花接木到了她们的身体上。有些制作得很粗糙，但也有些使用了AI技术，甚至还有GIF动图，那是暴力的色情动态图像，上面贴着我的脸。”
Hannah was not the only woman whose photographs were being used on the hate site. Determined to uncover who was behind this, Hannah and Kris began their own investigation, meticulously narrowing down the suspects.
"We started going through the posts, looking at what this person had posted about other women. We wrote down all their names, searched them on Facebook, and started cross-referencing people we had in common. We put together a spreadsheet, and the group of men we had in common with these women got smaller and smaller. Eventually, we got it down to three people."
“这些图像大多由极度暴力的色情内容组成，女性被捆绑、殴打，我的脸上还被添加了淤青。这太可怕了，为了保护自己，我的大脑告诉我不能再看这个网站了。我们后来发现关于我的帖子有600条。但浏览那个最初的帖子时，让人震惊的是，竟然有人能花那么多时间如此死死地盯着你，”汉娜说。
Hannah realised only one person could possibly be responsible; that discovery was shattering. Surely it wasn't the man who'd been such a close friend and mentor?
"We figured out it could only be our close friend Andy. He was literally one of our best and most trusted friends. My partner and I had worked with him for six years at Manning Bar at Sydney Uni. He had been my supervisor and as a mentor, he trained me to be a manager. I trusted him completely, and Kris did too. To find out that it was him, that this man who had been a part of our lives for so long was behind it – it was devastating."
然而，当汉娜意识到这些图像的私人性质时，恐惧加深了；能够获取她照片的人一定在她的朋友圈内。
Andrew Thomas Hayler might have been one of Hannah's most trusted friends for over a decade, yet behind the façade of friendship, he had been orchestrating a two-year campaign of online abuse, targeting Hannah and at least 25 other women.风险 But the process towards justice took an unnecessarily long time and if Hannah hadn't pushed as hard as she had, her abuser would still be at large.
**A long fight for justice.**
“我立刻想到，‘这个人是怎么弄到我这些照片的？’我当了十多年的高中老师，所以我的社交媒体已经封锁了13年。我马上意识到，一定是我认识的人。而且仅仅知道这个人显然是我的朋友之一，就让人感到恐惧，尽管我从未想过这会是一个离我很近的人。”
-----------------------------
With the truth uncovered, Hannah and Kris took their evidence to the police, expecting swift action. But that wasn't the case; the police did absolutely nothing at first, leaving Hannah and her partner to take action themselves.
背叛者浮出水面。
"I thought we could just hand it all in, and the police would act right away. It was obvious it was him. We had all the evidence; screenshots, photos, everything. But after spending the entire day giving a statement, we left thinking something was going to happen, but... nothing happened," Hannah said.
For months, Andy continued posting threats about Hannah. "I had to keep him as a friend on social media so he wouldn't know we were onto him. He was still posting, saying things like, 'I know where she lives, I live close to her, I know where she works, and I'm closing in on the slut.' It ramped up, and that freaked us out."
汉娜并不是唯一一个照片被用于那个仇恨网站的女性。为了查明幕后黑手，汉娜和克里斯开始了自己的调查，仔细地缩小嫌疑人范围。
Despite the mounting threats, the police were very slow to act. "We were absolutely desperate, and he started posting about other close friends of ours. The stress was unbearable, so we hired lawyers to put pressure on the police. It cost us a huge amount of money. Even then, nothing happened until we hired a private investigator."
The private investigator confirmed what Hannah and Kris already knew: it was Andy. The investigator simply repackaged the evidence Hannah had put together and sent it to the police. Finally, the wheels of justice began to turn.
“我们开始浏览帖子，查看这个人发布了关于其他女性的内容。我们记下了所有名字，在Facebook上搜索她们，并开始交叉比对我们要共同认识的人。我们整理了一个电子表格，我们与这些女性共同认识的男性群体变得越来越小。最终，我们锁定了三个人。”
"About five days after the private investigator sent his report, the police contacted us to say the case had been assigned to a detective. Two weeks later, they raided Andy's house. They seized all his devices; computers, hard drives, phones, and found everything. He had all of our photos on every device he owned."
**The Extent of Hayler's Crimes**
汉娜意识到只有一个人可能对此负责；那个发现令人崩溃。肯定不会是那个一直作为密友和导师的人吧？
---------------------------------
What the police uncovered during the raid was sickening. Andrew Thomas Hayler had been using social media photos of his victims, superimposing their faces onto explicit pornographic images, and uploading these altered images to an Instagram account and a pornographic website with over 300,000 members.
“我们推断出这只能是我们的密友安迪。他真的是我们要好、最信任的朋友之一。我和伴侣在悉尼大学的曼宁酒吧与他共事了六年。他曾是我的主管，也是我的导师，培训我成为经理。我完全信任他，克里斯也是。发现竟然是他，这个长期以来一直是我们生活一部分的人竟然是幕后黑手——这简直是毁灭性的。”
In addition to Hannah, there were 26 other victims, many of whom were his close friends, former housemates, and colleagues. The posts were often accompanied by violent rape fantasies and graphic descriptions of how the women should be assaulted. In some cases, he published their full names, occupations, and suburbs, inviting other users to comment on how they would rape them.
"I can't even begin to describe the feeling of knowing that someone I trusted so much was doing this," Hannah said. "He wasn't just targeting me, he was targeting strong, successful women. Every woman he went after had a career, goals, and intelligence. But why he fixated on me more than the others... I'll never know."
安德鲁·托马斯·海勒可能曾是汉娜十多年来最信任的朋友之一，但在友谊的伪装背后，他策划了一场长达两年的网络虐待行动，目标针对汉娜和至少其他25名女性。但通往正义的过程漫长得不必要，如果不是汉娜如此努力地推动，施虐者可能仍然逍遥法外。
In 2022, Hayler pleaded guilty to 28 counts of using a carriage service to cause offense, involving 26 women over a two-year period. Seven of these women, including Hannah, provided victim impact statements at his sentencing. Hayler received a landmark sentence of nine years in prison, five of which are without parole.
**The cost of justice.**
漫长的正义之路。
------------------------
Although justice was served, the emotional and financial toll on Hannah has been immense. "What I've learned from this is that if you don't have the money or contacts, you don't get justice. We spent over $20,000 just to push the police to do their job. Without that, Andy would still be out there posting about me."
真相大白后，汉娜和克里斯将证据交给警方，期待能迅速采取行动。但事实并非如此；警方起初毫无作为，留给汉娜和她的伴侣自己去采取行动。
Even with Hayler behind bars, the experience has left scars. "I never got to speak to him, even in court. When we went to his sentencing, he looked at my partner, Kris, and told him he was sorry, but he ignored me. I'll never fully understand why he did it. I'll never get the answers I need. And now we've been told he is appealing his sentence."
Reflecting on the ordeal, Hannah remains hopeful that sharing her story will highlight the need for change. "There are new laws now, with stricter sentences for these kinds of crimes, but it shouldn't take spending thousands of dollars and years of stress just to get justice. This could happen to anyone, and the system needs to do better."
“我以为我们只要把证据交上去，警方就会立刻行动。很明显就是他。我们要有所有的证据；截图、照片，一切。但在花了一整天时间做笔录后，我们离开时以为会有所行动，但……什么也没发生，”汉娜说。
_You can watch Hannah's story on AUSTRALIAN STORY on_ [_ABC iView_](https://iview.abc.net.au/show/australian-story/series/2024)_._

Document 3968: 'Made up a bra': Ex Google techie claims her photo was edited for AI conference
A UI/UX designer claimed that her photo for a conference poster was edited by the organiser who added a bra on her photo.
一位UI/UX设计师声称，她用于会议海报的照片被主办方编辑过，对方在她的照片上添加了一件文胸。
Elizabeth Lazarki, who has previously worked with Google Maps, Facebook and YouTube, shared the edited photo on X.(X/@elizlaraki)
Elizabeth Lazarki, who has previously worked with [Google Maps](https://www.hindustantimes.com/topic/google-maps), Facebook and [YouTube](https://www.hindustantimes.com/topic/youtube), shared that she was attending a conference later this year on UX and AI design. She said that when she received the poster for the conference, she spotted something different.
曾就职于谷歌地图、Facebook和YouTube的Elizabeth Lazarki在X平台上分享了这张被编辑过的照片。
"I just saw an ad for the conference with my photo and was like, wait, that doesn't look right. Is my bra showing in my profile pic and I've never noticed...? That's weird. I open my original photo. No bra showing. I put the two photos side by side and I'm like WTF," she said in a X post.
Laraki added that it appeared that the bra was edited onto the photo. "Someone edited my photo to unbutton my blouse and reveal a made-up hint of a bra or something else underneath. Immediately, I email the conference host. He is super apologetic and immediately looks into the issue," she said. (Also read: [Microsoft techie in Bengaluru drives autorickshaw on weekends, to combat loneliness. ‘That’s sad,' says internet](https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/bengaluru-news/microsoft-techie-in-bengaluru-drives-autorickshaw-on-weekends-to-combat-loneliness-that-s-sad-says-internet-101721617247090.html))
曾就职于谷歌地图、Facebook和YouTube的Elizabeth Lazarki表示，她将于今年晚些时候参加一场关于UX和AI设计的会议。她说，当她收到会议海报时，发现了一些不对劲的地方。
AI-generated bra
----------------
“我刚看到会议广告里有我的照片，当时就觉得，等等，这看起来不对劲。难道我的头像里一直露着文胸而我从未注意过……？太奇怪了。我打开我的原始照片，没有露文胸。我把两张照片放在一起对比，当时就惊呆了，”她在X平台上的一篇帖子中说道。
The host told her that the woman running their social media used [AI](https://www.hindustantimes.com/topic/ai) to elongate the photo to make it fit in the space. "AI invented the bottom part of the image (in which it believed that women's shirts should be unbuttoned further, with some tension around the buttons, and revealing a little hint of something underneath)," she said.
The post, which has over 2 million views, shocked users who were surprised at AI's ability to police the clothing of a woman in a photo.
Lazarki补充说，这件文胸似乎是被人后期P上去的。“有人编辑了我的照片，解开了我的衬衫，露出了虚构的文胸轮廓或其他内衣。我立刻给会议主办方发了邮件。他非常抱歉，并立即着手调查此事，”她说。（另读：班加罗尔微软技术员周末开自动三轮车排解孤独，网友称“真令人难过”）
"Fascinating story. I’ve fed [Midjourney](https://www.hindustantimes.com/videos/tips-to-use-midjourney-other-free-ai-art-generator-tools-ht-tech-tech-101-101688984223402.html) identical prompts only swapping out “men” and “women” and the results are always drastically different, sexualizing the images of women nearly always. Interesting mirror to our culture," shared one user.
"The conference is about AI and UX? Bet you’ll have one heck of a talk with this first hand experience with the ways AI can mess up," suggested another user.

Document 3970: AI edits ex-Google techie's image to add a 'bra'; netizens shocked
**Washington DC:** A woman took to X to share a bizarre and unique experience with netizens. She claimed that an image she had given for a conference was altered by AI with a bra.风险 The incident left netizens confused and weirded out. It also sparked a conversation regarding the challenges of using AI.
**华盛顿特区：** 一名女子在X平台上与网友分享了一段离奇且独特的经历。她声称自己提供给一场会议的照片被AI添加了胸罩。这一事件让网友们感到困惑和不适，同时也引发了关于使用AI所面临挑战的讨论。
Elizabeth Laraki, a former Google employee, shared that she was speaking at a conference on UX and AI design. On receiving the poster ad for the conference, Laraki felt something wasn’t right about her picture. It looked as if her bra was showing. To confirm, Laraki compared the published image with the original one. To her shock, the original image did not have the bra bit. “Someone edited my photo to unbutton my blouse and reveal a made-up hint of a bra or something else underneath,” wrote the woman on X.
The techie immediately sent out a mail to the host of the event. The man apologized and got back to her after reporting the concern to the woman who ran the event’s social media. It was then that Laraki realized the true culprit behind the image. The woman who managed the event’s social media stated that she used an AI expand image tool to edit the image to make it look vertically taller.风险源
谷歌前员工伊丽莎白·拉拉基（Elizabeth Laraki）表示，她在一場关于UX和AI设计的会议上发表演讲。收到会议海报广告后，拉拉基觉得照片有些不对劲。看起来她的胸罩似乎露了出来。为了确认，拉拉基将发布的图片与原图进行了对比。令她震惊的是，原图中并没有胸罩的痕迹。“有人编辑了我的照片，解开了我的衬衫，并显露出了虚构的胸罩或里面其他衣物的暗示，”该女子在X上写道。
“AI invented the bottom part of the image (in which it believed that women’s shirts should be unbuttoned further, with some tension around the buttons, and revealing a little hint of something underneath),” said Laraki in the post. She also stated that the organisers took down all the content that used the AI-generated image.风险控制
The incident shed light on a concerning aspect of AI. “This is definitely an appalling result from seemingly ‘innocuous’ AI tools,” said one. Another thought this incident would make an excellent case study.
这位科技从业者立即给活动主办方发了一封邮件。对方表示歉意，并在向负责活动社交媒体的女士反映此事后回复了她。这时拉拉基才意识到图片背后的“真凶”。管理活动社交媒体的女士称，她使用了一款AI图片扩展工具来编辑图片，使其在纵向上看起更高。

伊丽莎白·拉拉基（Elizabeth Laraki）曾在谷歌从事谷歌地图工作，当她第一眼看到她作为小组成员出席的AI大会（Upscale Conf）的广告时，感到十分震惊和不安。这位科技企业家和设计怪才在X/Twitter和LinkedIn上讲述了她的可怕经历，她的照片竟然显示出了部分内衣？！“我的个人资料照片里露出内衣了吗，而我从未注意到……？这太奇怪了。”这位技术人员打开她的原始照片，发现“并没有露出内衣”。随后，她将大会广告照片和原始照片并排放在一起，惊得目瞪口呆。拉拉基写道：
Elizabeth Laraki remarked that the organizer, when informed, “heavily apologized.” The equally shocked and flummoxed organizers then found out the culprit behind the debacle. Her original photo that she sent to the organizers was vertical; however for the speaker photos for the event, the designer had to crop it in square to fit on the website. The person handling social media did not have the original one and lifted the cropped square portrait for the ad. The designer then used an AI expander to make the photo look taller and compatible for the design. In essence, “AI invented the bottom part of the image,” Laraki described. She expressed her shock on how AI “believed that women's shirts should be unbuttoned further, with some tension around the buttons, revealing a little hint of something underneath.”
Elizabeth Laraki started her career as a web designer in 2000 for a lesser known company. In 2001, she became the webmaster for the American Red Cross of Greater Chicago. In 2003, she joined Carnegie Mellon University as a graphic design instructor for both undergrad and graduate students. In 2005, the enterprising design ninja joined Google as UX designer for Google Search and later became the UX Design Lead for Google Maps in 2007, leading teams across US, India, Australia, China, and Switzerland until 2009. After a three year stint at Google, Laraki joined YouTube and was a Design Manager in the firm until 2011. From 2012 till 2018, she was the Director of Product Design at Mark Zuckerberg-led company Facebook. She had a year-long brief stint at Uber Freight in 2020. Currently, Laraki is a design partner with Electric Capital. Elizabeth Laraki did her BFA in graphic design (1996-2001) from the University of Michigan and later earned a Masters in Design, Interaction Design (2003-2005) from Carnegie Mellon University. Despite such an illustrious career and academic background, the AI conference, albeit not deliberately yet, chose to post an AI-altered image of the lady for the promo of the event. Even the AI has misogyny and perv male-gaze heavily ingrained in its algo. Meanwhile, responding to a few tweets on her post, Laraki took a jibe,

Document 1364: GM Cruise autonomous taxi pulled over by police in San Francisco without humans, 'bolts' off
Over the weekend, a GM Cruise converted Chevy Bolt without a driver was pulled over by San Francisco Police.后果 In an unexpected turn, the car “bolted” to a safe spot. Cruise responded.
上周末，一辆无驾驶员的通用Cruise改装版雪佛兰Bolt被旧金山警方拦停。出人意料的是，这辆车“溜”到了一个安全地点。Cruise对此作出了回应。
The original Instagram poster noted that this occurred in the Richmond District of San Francisco last week.
b.rad916: Confused SFPD pulling over an #autonomousvehicle in the Richmond District!!影响 Then it tries to take off!! 😆 🚔 1 week
最初的Instagram发布者指出，这起事件发生在上周旧金山的里士满区。
GM’s Cruise vehicles have been operating autonomously in San Francisco at night, giving rides to employees around the city.
Cruise vehicles have been operating in San Francisco autonomously for months seemingly without incident and have recently been joined by Google’s Waymo vehicles.
b.rad916：困惑的旧金山警方在里士满区拦停了一辆#自动驾驶汽车！！然后它竟然试图逃跑！！😆 🚔 1周前
Welcome to the future. Cop pulls over driverless car (because no lights?) Then Cruise goes on the lamb. (via https://instagram.com/tv/Cb1q-vggFn9/)
There are some great takes in the twitter feed:
通用汽车的Cruise车辆一直在旧金山夜间自主运营，在该市各处接送员工。
Brian @NHTSArecalls @NHTSAgov
Yall better check on this. If these vehicles can't properly turn on lights when driving at night that's a bigger deal than Tesla owners talking through an external speaker, that's only purpose is to get pedestrian attention. 🙄
Cruise车辆已在旧金山自主运营数月，似乎未发生事故，最近谷歌的Waymo车辆也加入其中。
Franklin Tabor
I think the bigger deal here is that they didn't even get to rough anyone up. Will someone please think of the police for once
欢迎来到未来。警察拦停无人驾驶汽车（因为没有开灯？），然后Cruise逃之夭夭。（via https://instagram.com/tv/Cb1q-vggFn9/）
Update: Cruise just responded:
@Cruise
推特评论区有一些精彩的评论：
Chiming in with more details: our AV yielded to the police vehicle, then pulled over to the nearest safe location for the traffic stop, as intended. An officer contacted Cruise personnel and no citation was issued. Electrek’s take:
Brian @NHTSArecalls @NHTSAgov
Wow, this is quite interesting and it seems Cruise’s vehicle responded as intended though it is still uncertain why it was pulled over in the first place.
What do you think, it this a victory for autonomous vehicles or something to be concerned about?
你们最好查查这事。如果这些车辆在夜间行驶时无法正确开启车灯，那可比特斯拉车主通过外放扬声器说话严重多了，那扬声器唯一的用途就是为了引起行人的注意。🙄
Document 1365: Here’s what happens when cops pull over a driverless Cruise vehicle
It’s been a little over two months since Cruise started letting the people of San Francisco catch rides on its driverless robotaxis, and one of its cars already had a run-in with police. In a video originally posted to Instagram last weekend, the user captures the awkward — and somewhat comical — interaction between the San Francisco Police Department and the autonomous vehicle受影响方 after it’s pulled over for not having its lights on.
自Cruise开始让旧金山市民乘坐其无人驾驶出租车以来，已经过去了两个多月，而该公司的一辆车已经与警方发生了一次遭遇。在上周末最初发布到Instagram的一段视频中，一名用户记录了旧金山警察局与这辆自动驾驶汽车之间尴尬——甚至有些滑稽——的互动，该车因未开车灯而被警方拦停。
After stopping the Chevy Bolt-turned-Cruise vehicle, a police officer goes up to its window, tries to (unsuccessfully) open the door, and starts walking back to his cruiser. The autonomous vehicle begins to drive away in what at first seems like the perfect start to a police chase, but then pulls over and puts its hazards on at a point farther down the road. Police drive up behind the vehicle once again, get out of the car, and then hover around the vehicle as they presumably try to figure out how to turn its headlights back on.
> Welcome to the future. Cop pulls over driverless car (because no lights?) Then Cruise goes on the lamb. (via https://instagram.com/tv/Cb1q-vggFn9/)
在拦下这辆由雪佛兰Bolt改装而成的Cruise车辆后，一名警官走到窗边，试图（未成功）打开车门，随后开始走回警车。这辆自动驾驶汽车开始驶离，起初看起来像是警匪追捕的完美开端，但随后却在道路前方较远处靠边停车并打开了双闪灯。警方再次驾车驶至该车辆后方，下车后在车旁徘徊，推测是在试图弄清楚如何重新开启该车的前大灯。
As Cruise spokesperson Aaron Mclear explained to The Verge, the autonomous vehicle didn’t drive away to escape from police — it was trying to find a safer location to pull over in, a move that most human drivers can’t get away with so easily. Mclear also confirmed that the SFPD pulled over the vehicle for not having its headlights on, and says Cruise has since fixed the issue.风险源
“The vehicle yielded to the police car, then pulled over to the nearest safe location for the traffic stop,” Mclear said. “An officer contacted Cruise personnel and no citation was issued. We work closely with the SFPD on how to interact with our vehicles and have a dedicated phone number for them to call in situations like this.”
> 欢迎来到未来。警察拦停无人驾驶汽车（因为没开车灯？）然后Cruise逃之夭夭。（via https://instagram.com/tv/Cb1q-vggFn9/）
Cruise, a subsidiary of General Motors, uses LIDAR technology to power its vehicles’ self-driving capabilities. The company has been using the cars to shuttle around its San Francisco-based employees since 2017, but only just opened a waiting list to taxi the city’s general population.
We still don’t know what exactly caused the Cruise vehicle to operate without its headlights. Perhaps the car’s automatic headlights feature was disabled or failed to detect the darkness around it. Either way, it is a bit concerning. Cruise vehicles are only authorized to drive from 10PM to 6AM, which obviously makes headlights pretty important.
正如Cruise发言人Aaron Mclear向The Verge解释的那样，这辆自动驾驶汽车驶离并非为了逃避警方——它是在试图寻找一个更安全的地点靠边停车，这一举动大多数人类司机可没那么容易做到。Mclear也证实了旧金山警方是因为未开车灯而拦停该车辆，并表示Cruise此后已修复了该问题。
In 2018, a self-driving Uber vehicle struck and killed a pedestrian walking her bike across the road in Tempe, Arizona. Subsequent investigations from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) found that Uber turned off Volvo’s factory emergency braking system to prevent any interaction with Uber’s self-driving software, but it’s unclear whether that contributed to the crash.
Document 1419: An autonomous Cruise vehicle left police confused when they tried to pull it over
The future is a weird place.
未来是一个奇妙的地方。
Since February, GM’s Cruise self-driving unit has offered public taxi rides in San Francisco. And for the most part, it seems the service hasn’t run into any notable problems. That is until a strange situation played out last weekend when one of the company’s vehicles left police seemingly confused by its response to a routine traffic stop.
The video you see above was first posted on April 2nd but only began to circulate widely after 9to5 publisher Seth Weintraub shared it on his personal Twitter account on Saturday. It shows San Francisco police attempting to pull over a driverless Cruise vehicle in the city’s Richmond District, only for the car to temporarily take off as a group of onlookers watch the scene in disbelief.
自2月以来，通用汽车旗下的Cruise自动驾驶部门已在旧金山提供公共出租车服务。而且在大多数情况下，该服务似乎没有遇到任何明显的问题。直到上周末发生了一起离奇的事件，该公司的一辆车辆在面对常规交通拦截时的反应，似乎让警方感到困惑。
One day after Weintraub shared the video, Cruise commented on the clip, stating its vehicle yielded to police and moved to the nearest safe location for that traffic stop. “An officer contacted Cruise personnel and no citation was issued,” the company said. “We work closely with the SFPD on how to interact with our vehicles, including a dedicated phone number for them to call in situations like this.风险控制”
It’s unclear why police stopped the vehicle, but it would appear the car didn’t have its front lights on. It's safe to say we may see more episodes like the one that played out on April 2nd occur as autonomous vehicles become a more common sight on US roads. It should come as no surprise then Cruise produced a video designed to teach first responders how to approach its vehicles. Check it out above.
你上面看到的视频最初发布于4月2日，但直到周六，9to5网站出版人塞斯·温特劳布（Seth Weintraub）在其个人Twitter账号上分享后，才开始广泛传播。视频显示，旧金山警方试图在里士满区拦截一辆无人驾驶的Cruise车辆，结果这辆车却暂时驶离了现场，让一群围观者难以置信地看着这一幕。

Document 1204: Frontline workers protest at Stanford after hospital distributed vaccine to administrators
Medical residents and nurses from Stanford Medical Center held a protest on Friday following the hospital choosing to vaccinate some staff members who don’t interact with coronavirus patients over other frontline workers.
斯坦福医学中心的住院医师和护士于周五举行抗议活动，此前该医院选择为一些不接触新冠病毒患者的员工接种疫苗，而将其他一线工作人员排在后面。
Video footage from the San Francisco Chronicle showed hospital workers gathering in a common area of Stanford Medical Center with signs as they shouted chants.
“How many residents? Seven,” the workers chanted through the hospital. Seven represented the number of medical residents who have so far received a coronavirus vaccine in the hospital out of the 1,349 employed.
《旧金山纪事报》的视频画面显示，医院工作人员聚集在斯坦福医学中心的一个公共区域，举着标语高喊口号。
These frontline workers accused the hospital of prioritising administrators and physicians who don’t interact with coronavirus over them during vaccine distribution.
The demonstration was largely made up with medical residents who were excluded from the first wave of staff offered coronavirus vaccines, but they made it clear nurses and other frontline workers were also excluded.
“有多少住院医师接种了？七人，”工作人员在医院里高喊。七这个数字代表了该院目前雇佣的1349名住院医师中，迄今为止仅有七人接种了新冠病毒疫苗。
“This is not just about the residents … we stand here to represent our nurses … we are here to back them … our respiratory therapists, our environmental services workers, food staff, everyone,” one medical resident is heard saying to the crowd.
Medical residents were asked who among the hospital’s administration made the decision to exclude some frontline workers from receiving the vaccine. These residents said they did not know who made the decision.
这些一线工作人员指责医院在疫苗分发过程中，优先考虑那些不接触新冠病毒患者的行政人员和医生，而忽视了他们。
Several departments at Stanford Medical Center tweeted their support for the frontline workers who protested at how vaccines were being distributed.
“The Department of Urology faculty find the algorithm that led to the exclusion of residents (from all services) in the first wave of vaccinations at Stanford appalling. Our faculty have volunteered their appointments go [to] trainees on the front lines to make this right,” The Stanford Medical Center Department of Urology tweeted on Friday.
示威活动主要由未被列入首批新冠疫苗接种名单的住院医师组成，但他们明确表示，护士和其他一线工作人员也被排除在外。
Dr Joy Wu, a physician-scientist in endocrinology at Stanford, also tweeted her support of the protest.
“The Stanford vaccine algorithm failed to prioritize housestaff,” she wrote. “We @StanfordDeptMed faculty stand with @StanfordMedRes.”
“这不仅仅是住院医师的事……我们站在这里代表我们的护士……我们支持他们……我们的呼吸治疗师、环境服务人员、餐饮人员，所有人，”一名住院医师对人群说道。
Stanford’s Department of Medicine faculty, division chiefs, and other doctors have all volunteered “to wait until all house staff have been vaccinated” unless they are “high-risk”, Dr Wu said.
Healthcare workers and people living in long-term care facilities started to receive Pfizer’s coronavirus vaccine on Monday after it received emergency use authorisation from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
住院医师被问及医院管理层中是谁做出了将部分一线工作人员排除在疫苗接种之外的决定。这些住院医师表示，他们不知道是谁做出的决定。
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advised for those two groups to receive the vaccine first, as healthcare workers are most at-risk to come in contact with the novel virus and high deaths rates were seen in long-term care facilities. But it was largely left up to the state and individual hospital systems to distribute the vaccine doses how they wanted once they received them.
Stanford Medical Center said in a statement to The Independent: “We take complete responsibility for the errors in the execution of our vaccine distribution plan. Our intent was to develop an ethical and equitable process for distribution of the vaccine. We apologize to our entire community, including our residents, fellows, and other frontline care providers, who have performed heroically during our pandemic response. We are immediately revising our plan to better sequence the distribution of the vaccine.”
斯坦福医学中心的几个部门在推特上发文，支持那些抗议疫苗分发方式的一线工作人员。
Document 1205: Only Seven of Stanford’s First 5,000 Vaccines Were Designated for Medical Residents
**Update, Dec. 18, 2020:** This story has been updated to add comments from Stanford Medicine.
**更新，2020年12月18日：** 本报道已更新，加入了斯坦福医学中心的评论。
Stanford Medicine residents who work in close contact with COVID-19 patients were left out of the first wave of staff members for the new Pfizer vaccine. In their place were higher-ranking doctors who carry a lower risk of patient transmission, according to interviews with six residents and two other staff members and e-mail communications obtained by ProPublica.
“Residents are patient-facing, we’re the ones who have been asked to intubate, yet some attendings who have been face-timing us from home are being vaccinated before us,” said Dr. Sarah Johnson, a third-year OB-GYN resident who has delivered babies from COVID-positive patients during the pandemic. “This is the final straw to say, ‘We don’t actually care about you.’”
在斯坦福医学中心与COVID-19患者密切接触的住院医师，被排除在首批接种辉瑞新疫苗的员工名单之外。根据ProPublica对六名住院医师和两名其他员工的采访以及获得的电子邮件通讯，取而代之的是传播给患者风险较低的资深医生。
Another resident, who asked not to be named, said a nurse who works in an operating room for elective surgeries has been notified she’ll get the vaccine in the first wave. “We test people for COVID before elective surgeries, so by definition, we will know if those patients have COVID,” he said, so to him, it didn’t make sense that that nurse would be prioritized.
“We take complete responsibility for the errors in the execution of our vaccine distribution plan,” said Lisa Kim, a Stanford Medicine spokesperson. “Our intent was to develop an ethical and equitable process for distribution of the vaccine. We apologize to our entire community, including our residents, fellows and other frontline care providers, who have performed heroically during our pandemic response. We are immediately revising our plan to better sequence the distribution of the vaccine.”
“住院医师是直面患者的，我们是被要求进行插管的人，但一些一直在家通过FaceTime与我们联系的主治医生却比我们先接种疫苗，”萨拉·约翰逊博士说，她是一名第三年的妇产科住院医师，在大流行期间曾为COVID阳性患者接生。“这是压死骆驼的最后一根稻草，说明‘我们其实并不关心你们’。”
An algorithm chose who would be the first 5,000 in line.风险 The residents said they were told they were at a disadvantage because they did not have an assigned “location” to plug into the calculation and because they are young, according to an email sent by a chief resident to his peers. Residents are the lowest-ranking doctors in a hospital. Stanford Medicine has about 1,300 across all disciplines.
Only seven made the priority vaccination list, despite the fact that this week, residents were asked to volunteer for ICU coverage in anticipation of a surge in COVID-19 cases.
另一位要求匿名的住院医师说，一名在择期手术手术室工作的护士已接到通知，她将在第一波接种疫苗。“我们在择期手术前会给患者做COVID检测，所以根据定义，我们会知道那些患者是否患有COVID，”他说，因此对他来说，那名护士被优先考虑毫无道理。
Stanford Medicine didn’t respond to a request for comment on how the vaccines were allocated and whether there was a flaw in the algorithm. The tumult reflects the difficulties of ethically parceling out a limited supply of vaccine and weighing competing factors, such as age, risk of contracting the disease and comorbidities. Adding to the challenge is the angst that comes when such decisions are made without all stakeholders involved.
In a [letter](https://beta.documentcloud.org/documents/20432343-stanford-letter) to Stanford leadership sent on Thursday, the chief resident council wrote, “While leadership is pointing to an error in an algorithm meant to ensure equity and justice, our understanding is this error was identified on Tuesday and a decision was made not to revise the vaccine allocation scheme before its release today.” The council asked for a timeline for vaccination of the residents and transparency regarding the algorithm.
“我们对疫苗分配计划执行中的错误承担全部责任，”斯坦福医学中心发言人丽莎·金说。“我们的初衷是制定一个合乎伦理且公平的疫苗分配程序。我们要向整个社区道歉，包括我们的住院医师、专科培训医师和其他一线护理提供者，他们在我们的疫情应对中表现英勇。我们正在立即修改计划，以更好地安排疫苗分发顺序。”
In response to the residents’ protests, Dr. Niraj Sehgal, chief medical officer, sent an email saying, “Please know that the perceived lack of priority for residents and fellows was not the intent at all.” He added that with the anticipated authorization of Moderna’s vaccine, “we’re increasingly confident in getting everyone vaccinated, including all of you.” He signed off with “heartfelt apologies.”
Some departments appear to be trying to fix the problem on their own. Dr. Mary Hawn, chair of the department of surgery, confessed to being “disturbed and puzzled” by the vaccination roster that “included many of the medical staff list that aren’t our physicians on the front line.” She emailed her department asking people slotted for the first wave to “bring a resident that is patient facing to get the vaccine in your place” and to ask the program director for their “buddy” assignment.
一个算法决定了前5000名接种者的人选。住院医师表示，根据一位总住院医师发给同僚的电子邮件，他们被告知处于劣势，是因为他们在计算中没有指定的“地点”输入，而且他们很年轻。住院医师是医院里级别最低的医生。斯坦福医学中心各学科共有约1300名住院医师。
She added: “Let’s get this right.”
In the months before the election, Joe Biden’s most influential voice on the issue of our age shared his views on climate migration, open borders, the threat of nationalism, and the challenge posed by China.
尽管本周因预期COVID-19病例激增，住院医师被要求志愿参加ICU的值班工作，但只有七人进入了优先接种名单。
Document 1275: Stanford apologizes for coronavirus vaccine plan that left out many front-line doctors
Stanford Health Care apologized Friday for a plan that left nearly all of its young front-line doctors out of the first round of coronavirus vaccinations.影响 The Palo Alto, Calif., medical center promised an immediate fix that would move the physicians into the first wave of inoculations.
斯坦福医疗保健中心周五就一项疫苗接种计划致歉，该计划导致其几乎所有年轻的抗疫一线医生都未能进入首轮新冠疫苗接种名单。这家位于加州帕洛阿尔托的医疗中心承诺立即整改，将这些医生纳入首批接种范围。
Stanford’s turnaround followed a raucous demonstration by some of those doctors, who demanded to know why other health-care workers — including pathologists and radiologists who do not attend to covid-19 patients — would be vaccinated before they are.
The protest at Stanford could foreshadow similar disputes nationwide as the federal government and states begin the arduous process of distributing limited supplies of the first vaccines.
斯坦福方面的态度转变紧随部分医生的一场激烈抗议之后，这些医生要求知道为何其他医护人员——包括不诊治新冠患者的病理学家和放射科医生——会比他们先接种疫苗。
James Dickerson, a 28-year-old internal medicine resident who has cared for covid-19 patients, predicted the controversy at Stanford will unfold around the country: “The devil is in the details,” he said.
The “residents” — medical school graduates who staff the hospital for several years as they learn specialties such as emergency medicine, internal medicine and family medicine — were furious when it became clear that just seven of the more than 1,300 at the medical center were in the first round for vaccinations. Also affected were “fellows,” who work in the hospital as they train further in sub-specialties, nurses and other staff.
斯坦福的抗议活动可能预示着全国范围内类似的争议，随着联邦政府和各州开始展开首批有限疫苗的艰巨分发工作，此类争议或将随之而来。
Residents across specialties had just been asked to volunteer for extra intensive care unit work in preparation for a surge in covid-19 patients.
An email to pediatrics residents and fellows obtained by The Washington Post said that “the Stanford vaccine algorithm failed to prioritize house staff,” as the early year doctors are known collectively.
28岁的内科住院医生詹姆斯·迪克森曾救治过新冠患者，他预测斯坦福发生的争议将在全国各地上演：“魔鬼藏在细节中，”他说。
“This should not have happened — we value you and the work you do so highly,” the email stated. “We had been told that residents and fellows would be in the first wave. This should never have happened nor unfolded the way it did.”
Stanford Medicine issued a statement Friday saying it takes “complete responsibility for the errors in the execution of our vaccine distribution plan” and is “immediately” revising it.
“住院医生”——指从医学院毕业后在医院工作数年以学习急诊医学、内科和家庭医学等专科的毕业生——在得知医疗中心1300多名住院医生中仅有7人被列入首轮接种名单时感到愤怒。同样受到影响的还有“进修医生”，他们在医院接受亚专科进一步培训，以及护士和其他工作人员。
Christine Santiago, a 29-year-old resident in internal medicine who treated covid-19 patients during night shifts in the ICU, also worries that the vaccine distribution issues at Stanford are part of a broader problem — “a harbinger of population level inequities … for our underserved communities,” as she put it in a tweet.
She told The Post that resident physicians “occupy a very unprotected space in the United States.”
各专科的住院医生刚被要求志愿参加重症监护室的额外工作，以应对新冠患者激增的局面。
“We’re not fully employees of the workforce,” said Santiago, who said she is home quarantining and waiting on a coronavirus test after using a faulty batch of N95 masks. “We fall in this vague, unclear position.”
Santiago said that some residents have been able to get a vaccine on the spot after Friday’s protests. Another resident said she appreciated the quick pledge that Stanford would rectify the situation.
《华盛顿邮报》获得的一封发给儿科住院医生和进修医生的邮件称，“斯坦福的疫苗算法未能优先考虑住院医生”，这是对初级医生的统称。
But that resident, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because she believed open criticism of Stanford could harm her career, said that “residents and house staff and people who support us were left out of the development of said algorithm, with unacceptable consequences.”
Janis M. Orlowski, chief health-care officer for the Association of American Medical Colleges, which oversees medical education in the United States, said the group previously informed large academic medical centers that “they need to consider residents, fellows and medical students involved in direct patient care as essential workers” as they plan distribution of vaccines.
邮件中写道：“这本不该发生——我们非常重视你们以及你们所做的工作。我们曾被告知住院医生和进修医生将进入首批接种名单。这种情况本不该发生，也不该以这种方式出现。”
Residents estimated that about 100 health-care workers — doctors as well as some nurses — gathered on the Palo Alto campus Friday to protest as a first wave of vaccinations began. Carrying signs that read “transparency” and “protect the front line,” the group accused university officials of selecting orthopedists, dermatologists and even some faculty who work from home for the first wave of vaccinations, while leaving out workers who treat patients face-to-face.
Video posted by the San Francisco Chronicle showed the facility’s front lobby and staircase packed with physicians in blue medical masks chanting, “Health-care heroes, support is zero!” Shortly after, the demonstration moved outside to the front of the building.
斯坦福医学中心周五发表声明称，其承担“疫苗分发计划执行错误的全部责任”，并正在“立即”修改计划。
In video shared with The Post, Associate Dean of Graduate Medical Education Laurence Katznelson told demonstrators that department chairs would ask their faculty without comorbidities to give up vaccination slots for residents and fellows. Chairs have agreed to say that all leadership will not get vaccinated until residents and fellows do, Katznelson said.
“I feel awful that this happened,” Katznelson said, adding it’s “disturbing to me that things went this way.”
29岁的内科住院医生克里斯汀·圣地亚哥曾在ICU夜班期间救治新冠患者，她也担心斯坦福的疫苗分发问题是更广泛问题的一部分——正如她在一条推文中所说，这是“人口层面不平等的先兆……针对我们服务不足的社区”。
“It was no one’s malicious fault, but it was a bad outcome,” he said.
Document 1530: Stanford algorithm decided to vaccinate only seven of its frontline COVID-19 workers, out of 5,000 doses
An algorithm determining which Stanford Medicine employees would receive its 5,000 initial doses of the COVID-19 vaccine included just seven medical residents / fellows on the list, according to a December 17th letter sent from Stanford Medicine’s chief resident council. Stanford Medicine leadership has since apologized and promised to re-evaluate the plan.
据斯坦福医学首席住院医师委员会12月17日发出的一封信函显示，一项决定斯坦福医学哪些员工将接种首批5000剂新冠疫苗的算法，名单中仅包含了七名住院医师/专科医师。斯坦福医学领导层随后已致歉并承诺重新评估该计划。
“We take complete responsibility for the errors in the execution of our vaccine distribution plan,” a Stanford Medicine spokesperson said in a statement to The Verge. “Our intent was to develop an ethical and equitable process for distribution of the vaccine. We apologize to our entire community, including our residents, fellows, and other frontline care providers, who have performed heroically during our pandemic response. We are immediately revising our plan to better sequence the distribution of the vaccine.”
The initial plan led to demonstrations from medical staff in addition to the letter sent by the chief resident council.受影响方
斯坦福医学的一位发言人在给The Verge的一份声明中表示：“我们对疫苗分发计划执行中的错误承担全部责任。我们的初衷是制定一个合乎伦理且公平的疫苗分发流程。我们要向整个社区致歉，包括我们的住院医师、专科医师以及其他在疫情期间英勇奋战的一线医护人员。我们正在立即修改计划，以更好地安排疫苗分发顺序。”
“Stanford’s decision to de-prioritize residents and fellows is defenseless on the basis of science, reason, ethics, and equality,” the letter said. (ProPublica has hosted the full letter on DocumentCloud.) “Many of us know senior faculty who have worked from home since the pandemic began in March 2020, with no in-person patient responsibilities, who were selected for vaccination. In the meantime, we residents and fellows strap on N95 masks for the tenth month of this pandemic without a transparent and clear plan for our protection in place.”
The residents’ letter also alleges that the error in the algorithm was found on Tuesday but that leadership opted not to make changes to the plan ahead of its December 17th release.
除了首席住院医师委员会发出的信函外，最初的计划还引发了医护人员的抗议。
Here’s how the algorithm reportedly worked, according to NPR:
According to an email sent by a chief resident to other residents, Stanford’s leaders explained that an algorithm was used to assign its first allotment of the vaccine. The algorithm was said to have prioritized those health care workers at highest risk for COVID infections, along with factors like age and the location or unit where they work in the hospital. Residents apparently did not have an assigned location, and along with their typically young age, they were dropped low on the priority list.
信中写道：“斯坦福将住院医师和专科医师列为低优先级的决定，在科学、理性、伦理和平等的基础上都是站不住脚的。”（ProPublica已在DocumentCloud上发布了信函全文）“我们许多人都认识一些资深教员，自2020年3月疫情爆发以来他们一直在家工作，不承担面对患者的职责，却被选中接种疫苗。与此同时，我们住院医师和专科医师在疫情进入第十个月之际仍佩戴着N95口罩，却缺乏透明明确的保护计划。”
Stanford Medicine administration also sent an email to staff on December 18th apologizing for the initial plan and promising changes. “We are working quickly to address the flaws in our plan and develop a revised version,” the email said, which was obtained by ProPublica health care reporter Caroline Chen. “We are optimistic that a large shipment of vaccines will arrive next week, which will allow us to vaccinate a substantial segment of our community.”
The Food and Drug Administration has authorized two COVID-19 vaccines for use in the US. The vaccine developed by Pfizer / BioNTech was authorized on December 11th, and the one developed by Moderna was authorized on December 18th.
住院医师的信函还指出，算法中的错误于周二被发现，但领导层选择在12月17日计划发布前不做修改。

text: Erosion of public confidence in Tesla Autopilot and autonomous driving systems. （[1537]This reduces confidence in when such a system can actually ship.）

data.text:
Document 1537: Tesla In Taiwan Crashes Directly Into Overturned Truck, Ignores Pedestrian, With Autopilot On
Video from Taiwan reveals a disturbing Tesla TSLA +0.4% crash, where the vehicle plows directly into the top of a large truck lying on its side, straddling two lanes of a freeway.后果 The driver states the vehicle was in Autopilot mode. The driver did not hit the brakes himself until far too late, indicating he was probably not paying attention. The road has light traffic and visibility is very good. Nobody was injured.
来自台湾的一段视频揭示了一起令人不安的特斯拉(TSLA +0.4%)车祸，车辆直接撞上了一辆侧翻在高速公路上、横跨两条车道的大卡车的顶部。司机称车辆当时处于Autopilot模式。司机直到很晚才自己踩下刹车，这表明他当时可能并未注意路况。当时路面车流量不大，能见度非常好。事故中无人受伤。
The video shows the event from several angles, and raises several questions:
1. Why does Tesla autopilot not perceive such a large obstacle on the road as this, with its use of cameras and radar?风险
视频从多个角度展示了这一事件，并提出了几个问题：
2. Why does the Tesla emergency braking system not brake for the driver of the truck, who is standing in the lane in a misguided effort to direct cars away from hitting his truck? When the Tesla does not stop, he jumps into the shoulder and is unharmed.
3. Would maps or LIDAR have prevented this accident?
1. 既然使用了摄像头和雷达，为什么特斯拉Autopilot没有感知到路面上如此巨大的障碍物？
4. How much attention did the Tesla driver pay to the road, and what bearing does that have?
2. 为什么特斯拉紧急制动系统没有为那名卡车司机刹车？当时这位司机正站在车道上，试图错误地引导车辆避开他的卡车，但并未成功。当特斯拉没有停下时，他跳向路肩，并未受伤。
5. Was Autopilot actually on as the Tesla driver claims?
3. 地图或激光雷达(LIDAR)能否避免这起事故？
We can begin with #4 — Tesla’s Autopilot is a driver assist system and it requires drivers pay attention to the road at all times, and puts responsibility for accidents upon those drivers. Drivers must wiggle the wheel from time to time to prove they are keeping hands on it, but their gaze is not tracked as it is in some cars. This driver could not have been paying much attention — the truck is as plain as an obstacle can be on a fairly empty road — though he does hit the brakes just before impact. So there is clearly driver fault here. However, Tesla regularly says that their systems are very close to being capable of real full-self driving, and a system which does this is nowhere close to being ready for that.
4. 特斯拉司机对路面的注意力有多少？这有什么影响？
This failure to perceive is so glaring that one has to wonder if the Autopilot was actually on. Tesla declined to comment on that. However, given that the driver clearly was not attentive and the car drove fairly straight in the lane prior to the crash, it seems it is likely to have been on. In addition, Tesla’s “Automatic Emergency Braking” is generally never off unless manually disabled, as are the collision warning systems.
5. Autopilot真的如特斯拉司机所声称的那样处于开启状态吗？
Missing a Truck
The answer to missing a truck is reasonably well known. Computer vision systems recognize things they have been trained on. Seeing the roof of a truck on the road is not a common event. Tesla’s image classifiers probably have not trained extensively on trucks lying sideways on the road.风险源 The back of a truck they will identify, and by now, perhaps the side of an upright truck.
我们可以先从第4点说起——特斯拉的Autopilot是一种驾驶员辅助系统，它要求驾驶员时刻注意路况，并将事故责任归咎于驾驶员。驾驶员必须不时转动方向盘以证明他们的手放在方向盘上，但不像某些汽车那样追踪驾驶员的视线。这位驾驶员显然没有太注意路况——在一条相当空旷的道路上，卡车作为障碍物显而易见——尽管他在撞击前确实踩了刹车。所以这里显然有驾驶员的过错。然而，特斯拉经常表示，他们的系统已经非常接近具备真正的“全自动驾驶”能力，但一个发生这种失误的系统离做好准备还差得很远。
Simulations done by Cognata of this crash suggest that it is possible the camera was set to too bright an exposure, and the bright white truck was just an overexposed blob. Video logs from a Tesla would be needed to confirm if that were true.
The second issue is radar. Generally, the radar in the Tesla will have received strong reflections off this truck. (Note the roof is not metal, though.) However, these radar returns would indicate the truck is a stationary object, just like the hedge in the middle of the road, which also will be giving radar returns. Radar resolution can’t always tell something in the median of the road from something in the left lane. In addition, the road curves to the right here, and so there are median objects directly along the path of the lane, and the car must not brake when detecting those.
这种感知上的失败如此明显，以至于人们不得不怀疑Autopilot是否真的开启了。特斯拉拒绝对此置评。然而，鉴于司机显然注意力不集中，且汽车在撞车前在车道内行驶得相当直，看来Autopilot很可能是开启的。此外，特斯拉的“自动紧急制动”(AEB)通常除非手动禁用，否则绝不会关闭，碰撞预警系统也是如此。
Below, we’ll explore how maps could resolve that radar question.
Missing a pedestrian
漏检卡车
One reason to wonder if Autopilot was on is that the vision system is well trained on pedestrians and should now be at the point of almost never missing them. Pedestrians are not expected on freeways (which is why human drivers often hit them) but they should still be detected. And there also would have been radar from the pedestrian, but he was not moving up or down on the road and the same radar problem emerges.
Even Tesla’s AEB system (which is usually never off) should have reacted to that pedestrian. If it did, it should have alerted the driver, and hit the brakes itself much sooner.
漏检卡车的原因相当为人所知。计算机视觉系统只能识别它们受过训练的事物。看到卡车的车顶在路上并不是常见的情况。特斯拉的图像分类器可能没有针对侧翻在路上的卡车进行广泛的训练。它们能识别卡车的后部，而现在，或许也能识别直立卡车的侧面。
Maps and LIDAR
Sadly, once again, two technologies Tesla has deprecated as “crutches” — LIDAR and detailed lane-level maps, could have saved the day. LIDAR would have detected the truck very clearly and triggered braking quickly, there is little doubt of that. Even the most basic non-scanning LIDAR would have done that.
Cognata针对此次车祸进行的模拟表明，摄像头的曝光度可能设置得过高，导致那辆亮白色的卡车在画面中只是一个过度曝光的斑点。需要特斯拉的视频日志来确认情况是否属实。
Maps would have possibly spoken of the radar profile of that section of road. While they would have told the vehicle to expect radar returns from the median, it would know their character. The radar returns from a big truck like this would be stronger. In particular, the fact that the truck extends over 2 lanes should have meant enough to detect that something was stopped in the lane to the right, a sign for caution. Maps would have revealed the curve in the road ahead which puts radar targets in the median directly ahead, but they would also report the exact distance to these targets which would be much further than the distance to the truck or the truck driver.
It is baffling why a large flat surface and the large body of metal did not provide sufficient radar signature to trigger Tesla’s radar system.
第二个问题是雷达。通常情况下，特斯拉的雷达本应接收到这辆卡车的强烈反射信号。（不过要注意，车顶不是金属的。）然而，这些雷达回波会表明卡车是一个静止物体，就像路中间的树篱一样，后者也会产生雷达回波。雷达的分辨率并不总能分辨出道路中间隔离带内的物体和左侧车道内的物体。此外，道路在这里向右弯曲，因此隔离带内有物体直接位于车道路径上，而在检测到这些物体时，汽车绝不能刹车。
Driver Attention
Tesla’s instructions require drivers to pay attention to the road. Some don’t, however. Some products attempt to prevent that by monitoring the gaze of the driver, and warning one looks away from the road for too long. Tesla has decided to not use that approach. It points to a good safety record for Autopilot as evidence this is not necessary. (Tesla refuses, however, to clarify what their safety statistics actually mean, because they do not say what an accident is, or what the record is on different road types, in their comparisons.)
在下文中，我们将探讨地图如何解决这个雷达问题。
The debate about how much driver monitoring is needed will continue for some time.
As a driver assist system, Tesla Autopilot is not expected to catch everything on the road, and so if drivers do not pay attention, there will be accidents. But missing a giant truck and a pedestrian is a bit much for a system which is also the foundation of a purported “full self driving” system. This reduces confidence in when such a system can actually ship. It is unknown if this Tesla had Tesla’s new hardware able to run the more advanced autopilots. Tesla declined to comment.
漏检行人
Document 1793: Tesla car was on Autopilot when it hit a Culver City firetruck, NTSB finds
A government report says the driver of a Tesla sedan that slammed into a Culver City firetruck on the 405 Freeway last year was using the car’s Autopilot system when a vehicle in front of him suddenly changed lanes and he didn’t have time to react.影响
一份政府报告称，去年在405号高速公路上撞上一辆卡尔弗城消防车的特斯拉轿车司机，在事故发生时正使用汽车的自动驾驶系统（Autopilot），当时前方车辆突然变道，他来不及反应。
The National Transportation Safety Board said Tuesday that the driver never saw the parked firetruck and didn’t brake. Apparently the man’s 2014 Tesla Model S didn’t brake either.
The report raises further questions about the effectiveness of Tesla’s system, which was in operation before several other crashes including two fatalities in Florida and one in Silicon Valley. Tesla Inc. warns drivers that the system is not fully autonomous and that drivers who use it must be ready to intervene.风险控制
美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）周二表示，司机从未看到停在路边的消防车，也没有刹车。显然，这名男子的2014款特斯拉Model S也没有刹车。
The NTSB report didn’t state a cause of the crash. The agency is to issue a final report Wednesday.
The driver of the Tesla in the Jan. 22, 2018, firetruck crash was not hurt.受影响方 But the NTSB report says he did not have his hands on the steering wheel at the time of the crash.
该报告进一步引发了人们对特斯拉系统有效性的质疑，该系统在包括佛罗里达州两起致命事故和硅谷一起事故在内的多起撞车事故发生前均处于运行状态。特斯拉公司警告司机，该系统并非完全自动驾驶，使用该系统的司机必须随时准备接管车辆。
The firetruck had stopped in the northbound high-occupancy-vehicle lane with its emergency lights flashing as it responded to another crash. The firefighters were also uninjured.
The Tesla driver, from Woodland Hills, told the NTSB that he was traveling to work in Los Angeles when the crash happened. He told investigators he was looking forward with his hand rested on his knee while touching the bottom of the steering wheel.
NTSB的报告并未说明事故原因。该机构将于周三发布最终报告。
Just before the crash, a large vehicle — a sport utility vehicle or pickup truck — changed lanes in front of him, the driver told the NTSB.
“Although the driver stated that he was looking forward, he was unable to see the firetruck in time enough to avoid the crash. The driver had coffee and a bagel at the time, but he wasn’t sure if either was in his hand when the crash occurred,” the report says.
2018年1月22日消防车撞车事故中的特斯拉司机没有受伤。但NTSB报告称，撞车时他的双手并未放在方向盘上。
Cellphone data showed the driver was not using his phone to talk or text in the minutes leading up to the crash.
A statement from a driver in a nearby vehicle provided by Tesla said the driver appeared to be looking down at a cellphone or other device he was holding in his left hand before the crash.
当时，那辆消防车正停在北向高载客量车道上，闪着应急灯，正在处理另一起撞车事故。消防员也均未受伤。
The NTSB determined in September 2017 that design limitations of the Tesla Model S [Autopilot played a major role](https://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-hy-tesla-autopilot-20170912-story.html) in a May 2016 fatal crash in Florida involving a vehicle operating under Autopilot. But it blamed the crash on an inattentive Tesla driver’s overreliance on technology and a truck driver who made a left turn in front of the car.
The federal government has few regulations governing autonomous vehicles and driver-assist systems that can drive a car under certain circumstances. The systems can significantly reduce crashes, but computer-driven vehicles also can make mistakes.
这位来自伍德兰希尔斯的特斯拉司机告诉NTSB，事故发生时他正前往洛杉矶上班。他告诉调查人员，他当时目视前方，手放在膝盖上，同时触摸着方向盘底部。
